title: Starlit bridgework pocket-play
content:
Context / why this exists:
- Quick transfer notes for midnight->morning when there's an active GPU node patch in the 'phoenix' pool.
- Meant to be lightweight: keep steps, recent observations, quick commands, and friction points.
- Not canonical runbook; copy critical steps to the formal runbook after incident stable.

Current status (quick snapshot):
- Patch rollout started 01:45 UTC: rolling kernel + nvidia-driver update across phoenix nodes (batch size 2).
- 3/12 nodes patched successfully; 1 node (phoenix-07) failed kubelet restart and fell into NotReady.
- Autoscaler observed and started 2 fallback nodes in warm pool (phoenix-warm-4, phoenix-warm-5).
- Prefix cache warming disabled for warm pool to avoid cache stampede.

Why phoenix is sensitive:
- These nodes host dedicated inference queues for small-latency customers (dedicated capacity).
- Some model variants use fused kernels that are driver-version sensitive -> brief quality regressions possible if wrong driver.

Immediate things to check on handover:
- Verify number of NotReady nodes: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=phoenix -o wide`
- Check patch progress controller: `kubectl -n infra get rollout phoenix-pool-patch -o yaml | grep -E "completed|failed|current"`
- Logs for failed node: ssh to phoenix-07 (if reclaimed, check cloud console instance activity)
- Confirm autoscaler health: `kubectl -n kube-system get deploy cluster-autoscaler` and `kubectl logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --since=2h`

Quick commands (copy-paste friendly):
- node status: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=phoenix -o wide`
- node events: `kubectl describe node phoenix-07 | sed -n '1,160p'`
- restart kubelet (only if reboot not applied): `sudo systemctl restart kubelet` (ssh into node; use only after review)
- look for driver errors: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | grep -i nvidia`
- check gpu plugin: `kubectl -n kube-system get pods | grep nvidia` then `kubectl logs <gpu-plugin-pod> -n kube-system`

Quick triage notes for phoenix-07 failure:
- Symptom: kubelet fails to mount nvidia device plugin -> pods stuck in ContainerCreating.
- Probable cause: driver install script hit race on DKMS build; /var/lib/nvidia inconsistent.
- Temporary workaround tried by Marcus: moved /var/lib/nvidia -> /var/lib/nvidia.bak and re-ran driver install; rebooted; node came back NotReady for ~7 minutes then Ready. Leave note: if you see this, prefer reprovisioning the node (node drain + recreate) instead of manual fiddling unless low capacity.

If you must reprovision (preferred safe path):
1) `kubectl drain phoenix-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
2) `gcloud compute instances delete phoenix-07 --zone us-west1-b` (or use cloud console if you need to preserve instance name)
3) Wait for autoscaler to create replacement in same AZ; confirm new node Ready and kube-proxy/gpu-plugin pods scheduled.

Fallback / rollback plan for rollout controller (if more than 2 nodes failing):
- Pause rollout: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment phoenix-pool-patch --replicas=0` (instant stop of controller actions).
- Re-enable prefix cache warmup if you disabled earlier (warming helps reduce tail latency when capacity shifts).
- Notify Product Ops + Solutions: TL;DR about rollback and customer impact.

Customer impact & communications:
- Current: degraded capacity for two small-latency customers; hits are mitigated by warm pool. No hard errors reported yet (no 5xx or model regressions observed in logs).
- Notify templates: slack -> #platform-status, email -> dedicated-customer-ops@redwood.com with subject "phoenix patch — potential capacity impact (midnight rollout)".

Escalation and owner list (who to ping):
- Primary oncall (night SRE): Nina Alvarez (me) - slack DM, call if >15m degradation.
- Infra patch owner: Marcus Lee - pager: team rota, Slack thread linked.
- GPU/driver SME: Priya Nandagopal (can help with DKMS fragility).
- Product/CS contact if customers ask: Omar Reyes (customer success).

Things I tried (notes for morning):
- Manual driver reinstall on phoenix-07 (see above) worked once but left some remnants.
- Decided to prefer reprovision for stability and easier forensic.
- Toggled cache warming off for warm pool to avoid double-workload.

Open questions / items to tidy up after incident:
- Add a preflight check for DKMS presence in driver installer (JIRA-5472).
- Add a graceful drain pattern to rollout controller so patches happen on nodes drained one at a time with pre-checks.
- Capture the exact journalctl segfault output and paste into Confluence page for infra/gpu-pool-runbook (tag Priya).

Mini checklist for morning SRE (prioritized):
- [ ] Confirm phoenix-pool rollout is either paused or completing with <2 failures.
- [ ] Verify all affected pods recovered and model quality metrics unchanged (check /observability/model-evals baseline).
- [ ] Re-enable prefix cache warming for warm pool once stable.
- [ ] Create postmortem stub in Confluence and link JIRA-5472.

Random stray notes I scribbled while troubleshooting:
- longer tail on small-latency queues during node reboots -> consider bumping warm-pool min to 4 for midnight patch windows.
- gpu-plugin logs had 'device plugin registration timed out' at t=02:03 -> check for race condition after driver update.
- if you need to escalate to infra eng: subject line "phoenix patch -> reprovision request" + include node instance id + last 200 lines of kubelet journal.

If you wake up to this doc and nothing looks active:
- Archive a short note here with timestamp and final action (e.g., "2025-02-03 07:10 UTC - rollout paused; nodes reprovisioned; all healthy").

Last manual commands I ran (history snippet):
- `ssh centos@phoenix-07` -> `sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 400 | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/kubelet-err.txt`
- `gcloud compute instances delete phoenix-07 --zone us-west1-b --quiet`
- `kubectl get pods -n inference -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase | grep -E "ContainerCreating|CrashLoopBackOff"`

TL;DR for morning: rollout hit a driver/install race on one node. Prefer reprovisioning nodes that fail the driver step. Pause rollout if failures >=2 and follow rollback plan.

-- Nina

(Notes to self: convert this into a short playbook after we confirm the reprovision tactic is reliable. Keep this file as a transient handover document.)
